subject: Civil Engineering
title: Steel Ribs and Lattice Girders
description: A short lesson to help you apply Steel Ribs and Lattice Girders.

hook.text: In weak ground, shotcrete alone isn't enough — steel ribs provide an internal skeleton.

buildup.text: Curved steel I-beams are erected against the tunnel profile — then shotcrete encases them.

discovery.text: Lattice girders — lighter, triangulated frames — replaced heavy ribs in many applications.

twist.text: The combination works like reinforced concrete — steel handles tension, shotcrete handles compression.

climax.text: In squeezing ground — clay under high stress — ribs may need to be installed every 2 feet.

punchline.text: Steel frames give shotcrete a backbone in ground too weak to stand alone.

quiz.question: Why are steel ribs used alongside shotcrete in weak ground?
options: Steel ribs are decorative elements required by architectural standards
They provide an internal skeleton that reinforces the shotcrete where ground is too weak
Steel ribs replace the need for rock bolts in all conditions
